provenance_note: Every state on this page is derived from the records' shape. Nothing journals §24 transitions and no §56.2 resolution has been recorded, so no Warrant can read above `would_satisfy` and no requirement above `in_progress` until a human signs.

release.note: Revision 0.1.0 is ACCEPTED (§101.2) and normative. A Warrant compiles against the revision its authorization recorded (§14), so a later revision does not move an authorized contract: 21 against 0.1.0.

requirements.title: This SAS is accepted by a human signature and every Warrant pins the accepted revision
Every Warrant is authorized and resolved by a human, never by the performer
Every resolution rests on an independent verification and recorded gate evidence
Every supported notation normalizes to the canonical GameRecord/GameState or fails explicitly; nothing is silently repaired or invented
Every supported export format round-trips: state, export, ingest, identical canonical state, proven on fixtures
Every GameRecord carries source and history_complete as source assertions; a four-field FEN source never yields history_complete true
Standard chess and Chess960/DFRC are first-class in ingest, replay, facts and export, in both UCI castling flavors
The viewer is Rust-only, Leptos and axum compiled to WASM, with no JavaScript or TypeScript in the application
An engine is reachable only as teacher labeler, post-decision scorer or opponent; the model's inference path never queries an engine
The player is exposed as a UCI engine, and an illegal model move is a reported failure, never silently corrected
Training corpora carry provenance and pass split audits before use; teacher labels are recorded as labels only
Model ability is reported per scoring axis with bounded evidence; no composite winner score and no scored free prose
A Burn-native model is admitted only through the parity gates, with reset isolation between inference passes

obligations.id: OBL-001: a v3 database moves its sessions aside and keeps its games
obligations.scope: the `sessions` → `legacy_sessions` step of `migrate_v4`, applied to a database at version 3 that holds one session row. No claim about payloads written by a later version, and none about downgrading.

obligations.id: OBL-002: a board write carries a revision, and a stale one is refused
obligations.scope: writes through the repository with an `expected_revision`. Concurrent writes that omit a revision are outside this claim.

obligations.id: OBL-003: a locked or published board refuses a write and offers a copy
obligations.scope: writes attempted against a board whose mutability is `locked` or `published`. Reading, exporting and copying are outside the claim.

obligations.id: OBL-004: a board has one parent, and reparenting moves it
obligations.scope: the one-parent rule at the repository. It says nothing about what the frontend does with a board whose parent changed underneath it.

obligations.id: OBL-005: studies keep chapters, versions and progress apart
obligations.scope: chapter ordering, version copies and per-chapter progress as the repository stores them. No claim about the editor UI.

obligations.id: OBL-006: the reset is announced once, and the old rows stay
obligations.scope: the notice a person sees after the v4 reset, and retention of `legacy_sessions`. Nothing about an old payload's content beyond counting it.

obligations.id: OBL-007: a session payload above the limit is refused, not truncated
obligations.scope: `PUT /api/session` with a payload over 2 MB is rejected; what the client does with the rejection is outside the claim.
